messages.author: f767f57fb3113a98
messages.subject: Assessing and interpreting standardized estimates
parts:
Hello,

I aim to assess the predictive role of  the regressions from the attached model (4net.R).  I had in mind a Bayesian SEM metric equivalent/similar to Cohen d' in the frequentist approach.

One comment received elsewhere
https://github.com/easystats/effectsize/issues/420

Pointed that the standardized coefficients provide what I am looking for.

zpost <- standardizedPosterior(fitModel.a1.bayes)
zpost <- as.data.frame(zpost)

# Then pass the draw to bayestestR for better organizing the output :
bayestestR::describe_posterior(zpost)

According to the results (see attached "res.output.xlsx" file), would  the "median" values provide such predictive assessment (e.g.,  similar to cohen d?). If so, should I transform them to any scale?  The regressions (but not the corr covariates) seem to be between 0 and 1 though. 

Thank you very much in advance for your comments.

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Assessing and interpreting standardized estimates
parts:
Julian

how would you get a cohen d in frequentist regression? As mentioned in the thread you posted, cohen d is more for mean differences, not regression effects. If you can show us how you would get this from a lavaan object we can translate to blavaan

Otherwise, from those standardize results I would recommend to interpret the regressions as the standardize regression slopes
